title: Mitigate SLO alert avalanches via impact-weighted silencing and dynamic hysteresis
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
Recent capacity regressions and a cascading autoscaler oscillation on 2026-02-18 produced an avalanche of burn-rate pager alerts across multiple SLOs (generation latency and error-rate). The alerts amplified through noisy deduplication and naive burn thresholds, causing wide paging churn and noisy oncall fatigue.

Goal:
Implement an impact-weighted silencing layer plus dynamic hysteresis on burn-rate/pager triggers to reduce multicluster alert avalanches while preserving detection of true degradations. The plan must be safe to roll out gradually (canary), observable, reversible, and compatible with existing SLO grouping.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Introduce an impact score for each burn alert that considers request volume, downstream customer routes, and estimated revenue-sensitive tokens. Only high-impact alerts will immediately page; medium/low impact alerts enter a short evaluation window.
- Add dynamic hysteresis: repeated short spikes should decay so a single transient burst does not immediately re-trigger paging for the same fingerprint for N minutes.
- Implement a cooldown and rolling count to avoid alert storms from autoscaler thrash.
- Provide dashboards and runbook entries that show suppressed alert counts, missed pages, and a backfill replay to validate detection fidelity.
- Can be toggled per-environment and per-customer tier (hosted vs dedicated).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Impact-weighting lets us retain sensitivity for high-business-impact signals while suppressing lower-priority noise; risk is that an unusual high-latency event on a low-volume route may be delayed. Mitigation: the evaluation window default is short (90s) and has an opt-in immediate page for routes marked critical.
- Hysteresis adds complexity to reasoning about SLO burn windows; we'll surface timelines in the console and add a visualization of 'alert eligibility' state.
- We prefer to change orchestration-layer alerting rather than re-tune all individual SLO thresholds across teams. This provides a single safety control but requires careful rollout.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation (week 1): add impact score computation in the alert evaluation service; emit metric "slo.alert_impact_score" with tags (slo, route, customer_tier).
2) Engine changes (week 2-3): implement silencing state machine with hysteresis and cooldown; ensure deterministic fingerprinting to dedupe alerts.
3) Safety & canary (week 4): expose feature flagging by customer_tier + region; run canary on non-production tenants then a small set of low-risk customers.
4) Observability & audit (week 4-5): dashboards, alert replay job, and oncall runbook updates. Create automated checks that verify total pages decreased while true-positive detection did not regress by >5% on holdout tests.
5) Rollout (week 6): phased enablement across hosted regions and Dedicated clusters; communication to customers and internal SRE/SE teams.

Artifacts and links:
- Postmortem: https://intranet.redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-02-18-autoscaler-oscillation
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/impact-weighted-silencing
- Prototype PR with evaluation metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/421
- Replay job notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.ai/alert-replay/impact-replay.ipynb

Risks and mitigations:
- False negatives: keep conservative defaults; run replay against historical incidents and maintain an 'immediate page' override for critical routes.
- Complexity for oncall: provide a one-click view in Console showing suppressed alerts and why they were held; ship training docs.
- Metric noise: start with coarse-grained impact buckets (high/medium/low) and refine after telemetry.

Next steps (owner: Diego Morales):
- Finalize proto schema for impact_score and commit initial instrumentation (due 2026-03-08).
- Implement silencing state machine prototype behind a feature flag (due 2026-03-15).
- Schedule canary with SRE for 2026-03-20 and prepare runbook updates.
